newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius bourse index climbs in lower volume.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius bourse index climbs in lower volume.

text.p: The Mauritius bourse index, Semdex gained 3.43 points to 323.24 on Wednesday, reflecting a broad rise across the market, brokers said.
Turnover was lower at 5.93 million rupees on 225,797 shares from 11.96 million rupees on 366,691 shares on Monday.
The Semdex rose for the fifth consecutive session on Wednesday from its late October year low of 305.41 points, as share prices were still seen attractive by investors, brokers said.
"Fundamentally speaking, there are good buys on the market judging from price earning ratios and dividend yields. This shows how low the market reached a couple of weeks back," one broker said.

The Semdex reached its year low level at the end of 19 consecutive bearish trading sessions as investors lacked confidence towards local politics which was characterised by the absence of a finance minister in the country since August.
But market sentiment then staged a turnaround on announcement that a new country fund would invest $15 million in the bourse.
On Wednesday, the majority of listed stocks rose, especially those of leading companies in the commerce and hotel sectors, thereby sustaining the Semdex rise.

Conglomerates Rogers was up one rupee to 87 on 2,828 shares and Ireland Blyth gained 30 cents to 14 rupees on 2,788 shares. Oil concern Shell (Mauritius) was 20 cents higher to 13.20 rupees on 700 shares but Happy World Foods lost 10 cents to 14.50 rupees on 5,377 shares.
New Mauritius Hotels climbed 50 cents to 29 rupees on 37,350 shares and Grand Baie Hotel added 30 cents to 34.50 rupees on 2,000 shares.

National airline Air Mauritius gained 30 cents to 52 rupees on 22,200 shares. Mauritius Commercial Bank was unchanged at 73 rupees on 13,050 shares and State Bank of Mauritius remained at 8.60 rupees on 20,500 shares.

Mauritius Union Assurance (MUA) was quoted ex-bonus and ex- rights on Wednesday at 28.80 rupees from 47 rupees on Monday but without any traded volume. MUA made a bonus issue of one share for every two shares held. This was followed by a rights issue of one share at 20 rupees for every three held.

Mauritius Breweries rose three rupees to 125 on 230 shares on anticipation that beer sales in Mauritius would rise for the end of year festivities. Sugar stock Mon Tresor Mon Desert was 60 cents higher to 36.20 rupees on 10,032 shares.
In the investment sector, National Investment Trust gained 20 cents to 11.40 rupees on 44,200 shares and Promotion And Development (PAD) climbed 80 cents to 14.80 rupees on 200 shares.
